network_graph_explainer:
This graph is generated step by step whenever new posts are loaded into the feed.
          Nodes represent posts (as images) and users (as user names).
          The size of the post images scales with the EdgeRank score of the post, i.e. if a post appears higher up in your feed, the image will be displayed larger.
          Users you follow are displayed in black, all others in gray.
          Green edges represent comments, red edges represent likes, gray edges show who created the post.
          You can move the displayed area with the mouse using drag & drop and zoom with the mouse wheel.
new_post_available_at: You can create a new post at {{time}}.
newsfeed_advertisement_settings_explaine: The advertising display in the newsfeed works according to a different algorithm than the normal posts. Here you can set how often an advertisement should be displayed
newsfeed_algorithm_3_customization_expla:
Algorithm 3 calculates an EdgeRank value for EVERY post (i.e. also for posts from users you do not follow). This EdgeRank value is calculated by the product of the popularity score, affinity score and time factor score of the respective post. Each of these three components consists of one or more so-called signals. 
 You can use the sliders to adjust how important each signal should be in the calculation. You will then see all posts in your newsfeed, sorted in descending order by EdgeRank value, i.e. the higher the EdgeRank value of a post, the higher up this post will appear in your feed.
newsfeed_ranking_metadata_update_explain: The ranking metadata is only updated when you refresh the page
newsfeed_post_affinity_score_explainer: This value describes the relationship between you and the creator of the post. The higher this value is, the better your relationship is. The value is calculated by the number of posts you have liked from the creator and the number of comments you have written under the creator's posts. If the post comes from a user you follow, an additional weight will be added. Here you can change three parameters to adjust the desired importance of the individual signals.
newsfeed_post_affinity_like_count_explai: How many posts of {{username}} have you liked
newsfeed_post_affinity_comment_count_exp: How many comments have you written under posts of {{username}}
newsfeed_further_settings_explainer: Here you can find further settings for customizing your newsfeed
newsfeed_followed_only_mode: Only shows posts from followed users in your newsfeed
newsfeed_post_time_factor_score_explaine: This value describes how recent the post is. Here you can use a slider to set the parameter t, which determines how much influence the age of a post has on the ranking. The higher this parameter is set, the lower the Time Factor Score for older posts: meaning the older posts are more penalized in the ranking, when this parameter is greater.
newsfeed_post_popularity_score_explainer: This value describes how popular the post is. The higher this value is, the more popular the post is. The value is calculated by the total number of likes and comments the post has received. Here you can change two parameters: how important should likes or comments for the computation of the popularity score be.
